thread:
Rowan: Heads-up — seeing a cluster of tiny GPU pod evictions in ap-south1 for ~22m. Packing index fell and short jobs are getting rescheduled a lot.
Leah: Any node events or volume attach logs?
Rowan: Events show repeated FailedAttachVolume + transient NodeNotReady: `attach failed: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded` then `Node ap-south1-wp-03 NotReady (NetworkUnavailable)`.
Diego: That pattern -> kubelet taints then scheduler immediately scatters tiny pods. Fragmentation spikes. Our nodeFlipGrace is only 12s which seems too short for attach RPC hiccups.
Infra-bot: Alert: evictions-high (cluster/ap-south1) firing.
Leah: Cost implication?
Rowan: Quick calc: ~6% extra GPU-hours on that warmpool the last 3h. If sustained, >$X/hr.
Diego: Short-term mitigation: canary bump kubelet attachTimeout to 40s on warmpool nodes and enable delayed-taint-lift so scheduler doesn't evict immediately on brief net blips. Also consider a warmpool-scoped scheduler patch: nodeFlipGrace=30s and reduce preempt aggressiveness for tiny-pod class.
Rowan: Proposed plan: 1) apply kubelet canary to warmpool-canary-1, 2) if good after 10m apply scoped scheduler softening to canary only, 3) monitor evictions, packing index, and cost for 20m, 4) roll out or rollback.
Ops-automation-bot: I can patch the canary kubelet config: `kubectl patch cm warmpool-canary-1-kubelet -n infra --patch '{"data":{"attachTimeout":"40s"}}'` then apply scheduler tweak scoped by node label. Auto-revert options available.
Leah: Let's try the kubelet canary first. Capture NIC firmware/kernel and cloud attach traces in parallel.
Rowan: Applying canary now. Will report back in 12m.
Infra-bot: Evictions-high cleared for cluster/ap-south1 (canary shows improvement).
Diego: Canary shows evictions down ~60% and more co-located tiny pods. Good signal. Follow-ups: infra/attach-investigate (collect driver logs, provider RPC latency), ops/scheduler-ci (simulate 10-25s NotReady flaps), and cost/impact note.
Leah: Assigning Diego for rollout and infra ticket. Thanks everyone.
